subject: problems with ipoints() and inla.spTransform() when using S^2 mesh in Cartesian xyz

messages.author: 8ec11560d71c3d45
messages.subject: problems with ipoints() and inla.spTransform() when using S^2 mesh in Cartesian xyz
parts:
Hi all,

Apologies if this is a trivial enquiry. I am a new user to INLA and have been trying to use inlabru::ipoints(samplers, domain,…) to generate integration points.

Our samplers is a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame (called “sp”) in lat-lon coordinates, and the domain is an inla.mesh object (called “mesh1”) on the sphere (S^2) in Cartesian geocentric xyz coordinates. The reason that our mesh is in Cartesian xyz is we are modelling global processes, so our mesh has to be on S^2. We find we have to supply loc= Cartesian, geodetic xyz coordinates to inla.mesh.2d() to make meshes with full global coverage (i.e. to have longitude-wrapping and equal area). The inla.mesh.2d function seems to project lon-lat locations onto R^2.  

When I ran ipoints(samplers=sp, domain=mesh1, group=”index”), I got the error “sp::over(samplers, integ_sp, returnList = TRUE) : identicalCRS(x, y) is not TRUE”. Then I tried to use inla.spTransform(mesh1, inla.CRS("longlat")) to make mesh1 have the same CRS as the SpatialPolygons, but I got the error “'crs0' is an invalid coordinate reference object”.

Does anyone know whether inla transformation function is possible to transform a S^2 mesh object in Cartesian xyz to a S^2 mesh in lon-lat? If it is possible, what would be the correct way to do that?

Thank you very much. Any guidance will be much appreciated!

Best wishes,

Xueqing

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with ipoints() and inla.spTransform() when using S^2 mesh in Cartesian xyz
parts:
Hi,

The ipoints function doesn't have full support for global meshes yet,
as it relies on conversion to a flat equal-area projection to compute
the integration weights.
I hope to soon have a new ipoints version to properly support this use case.

What kind of region is your sampler? What coordinate system is it stored in?
It's possible this issue can't be fully solved until we get more of
the more general sf support working.

For debugging purposes only:
Can you please try the mesh transformation with
inlabru::fm_spTransform() instead of inla.spTransform() and let me
know if that makes a difference or not?
It wouldn't give a usable mesh, but it should be able to do the
coordinate transformation.

A potential workaround would be to make an integration scheme for the
entire mesh, with the mesh nodes as integration points; something like
this:

ips_sphere <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(mesh$loc, data=data.frame(
weight = inla.mesh.fem(mesh)$va * earth.radius^2
), crs = fm_CRS("sphere"))
ips_globe <- fm_spTransform(ips_sphere, fm_CRS("globe"))

and then filter out the points outside the polygon, with a direct call
to sp::over. That way, the mesh wouldn't need to be involved in the
coordinate transformations.

For full integration accuracy along the sampler boundary, this step
needs to be done before aggregating the integration points, but it
might be sufficient as a temporary workaround.

I'll put this as an inlabru github issue to keep track of it.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with ipoints() and inla.spTransform() when using S^2 mesh in Cartesian xyz
parts:
Hi Finn,

Thank you so much for the quick response. We will try the potential workaround as suggested.

Our sampler is a SpatialPolygonDataframe. Each row in the data is a polygon area, and the observation values are area-averages over a polygon area. The coordinate reference system is “+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84”. Here I attached an example for simulating our sampler.

In addition, I just realized that the coordinate reference system (crs) information for our mesh was somehow left out and so mesh$crs is NULL. After clearly specifying a CRS to the mesh, both inlabru::fm_spTransform() and inla.spTransform() are able to do the coordinate transformation.

Best wishes,

Xueqing

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with ipoints() and inla.spTransform() when using S^2 mesh in Cartesian xyz
parts:
The mesh transformation may _run_, but the resulting mesh isn't usable
for _correct_ computations, as it becomes a deformed flattened mesh
that folds in on itself.
The correct solution is to transform and calculate on the sphere
instead of in projections; no projection handles the full globe
properly.

I have a PhD student who's working on polygon-aggregated data
problems, and coe for this will be making its way into the package.

Finn
